title: Scaffold proteins as dynamic integrators of biological processes.
authors: DiRusso, Christopher J; Dashtiahangar, Maryam; Gilmore, Thomas D
one_liner_zh: 综述支架蛋白构象变化在信号通路中的整合作用，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Scaffold proteins act as molecular hubs for the docking of multiple proteins to organize efficient functional units for signaling cascades. Over 300 human proteins have been characterized as scaffolds, acting in a variety of signaling pathways. While the term scaffold implies a static, supportive platform, it is now clear that scaffolds are not simply inert docking stations but can undergo conformational changes that affect their dependent signaling pathways. In this review, we catalog scaffold proteins that have been shown to undergo actionable conformational changes, with a focus on the role that conformational change plays in the activity of the classic yeast scaffold STE5, as well as three human scaffold proteins (KSR, NEMO, SHANK3) that are integral to well-known signaling pathways (RAS, NF-kappaB, postsynaptic density). We also discuss scaffold protein conformational changes vis-a-vis liquid-liquid phase separation. Changes in scaffold structure have also been implicated in human disease, and we discuss how aberrant conformational changes may be involved in disease-related dysregulation of scaffold and signaling functions. Finally, we discuss how understanding these conformational dynamics will provide insight into the flexibility of signaling cascades and may enhance our ability to treat scaffold-associated diseases.
abstract_zh: 支架蛋白作为多种蛋白质对接的分子枢纽，组织起高效的功能单元以支持信号级联反应。超过300种人类蛋白质已被表征为支架蛋白，在多种信号通路中发挥作用。尽管“支架”一词暗示了一种静态的支持平台，但现已明确，支架并非简单的惰性对接站，而是能够发生构象变化，从而影响其依赖的信号通路。在本综述中，我们整理了已被证明会发生可作用构象变化的支架蛋白，重点关注构象变化在经典酵母支架STE5活性中的作用，以及三种人类支架蛋白（KSR、NEMO、SHANK3）在已知信号通路（RAS、NF-kappaB、突触后密度）中的核心作用。我们还讨论了支架蛋白构象变化与液-液相分离的关系。支架结构的变化也与人类疾病相关，我们探讨了异常构象变化可能如何参与疾病相关的支架及信号功能失调。最后，我们讨论了理解这些构象动态如何为信号级联的灵活性提供洞见，并可能增强我们治疗支架相关疾病的能力。
